blocks.content: Inner join covered keeping only the genuine overlap between two tables. Left join covers a genuinely important variation, keeping every row from one specific table, the left table, regardless of whether a genuine match exists in the other table at all.

This topic covers exactly how a left join fills in missing data when no match exists, a genuinely common pattern for finding unmatched rows using a left join combined with a NULL check, and a specific, common mistake that can silently undo the entire point of using a left join in the first place.

blocks.alt: Left join covers keeping every row from one specific table, the left table, regardless of whether a genuine match exists on the other side

blocks.content: 1. Inner Join Versus Left Join

Inner join, covered in the previous topic, keeps only rows with a genuine match on both sides, which genuinely loses customers with zero orders entirely, since there is no matching order row for them to pair with.

Left join keeps every row from the left table, matched or not, which genuinely keeps customers with zero orders in the result, just with NULL values filled into whatever order related columns were selected, since no real order data actually exists for them.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784036197121-27850337.png
blocks.alt: Inner join loses customers with zero orders entirely; left join keeps every customer, filling order fields with NULL when no match exists

blocks.content: 2. What a Left Join Actually Does
blocks.text: 2. What a Left Join Actually Does

blocks.content: A left join genuinely keeps every row from the left table unconditionally, regardless of whether any matching row exists in the right table at all. It matches right table rows wherever a genuine match actually exists, exactly like an inner join would.

And critically, wherever no genuine match exists in the right table, a left join fills every selected right table column with NULL, rather than simply omitting that left row from the result the way an inner join genuinely would.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784036198825-560614669.png
blocks.alt: A left join keeps every left table row, matches right table rows where they genuinely exist, and fills right columns with NULL where no match exists

blocks.content: 4. Finding Unmatched Rows

A genuinely common, practical pattern combines a left join with a NULL check to find rows on the left side that have no genuine match at all, exactly the customers a plain inner join would have silently excluded.

SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

FROM customers c

codes.sql:

FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

blocks.content: This query genuinely isolates only the customers with zero orders, since the WHERE clause specifically keeps rows where the right table id came back NULL, exactly the signal that no genuine match was actually found for that particular customer.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784036202136-586031006.png
blocks.alt: Finding unmatched rows: a left join combined with a WHERE clause checking for NULL genuinely isolates rows with no match on the right side

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.content: Filtering on a right table column in WHERE without accounting for NULL, which can silently undo the entire point of the left join, since a plain condition on a right table column, without an explicit NULL check, effectively excludes every unmatched left row again.
5. Which Side Actually Matters
The table listed first, immediately before the LEFT JOIN keyword, is genuinely the left table, and every one of its rows is genuinely preserved in the final result, regardless of matching.

The table listed after LEFT JOIN is genuinely the right table, and only its matching rows are genuinely included, unmatched right table rows are simply not part of a left join result at all, a detail that matters a great deal once you are choosing between left join and its mirror image, right join, covered directly next.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784036203609-938776029.png
blocks.alt: The table listed first is the left table, with every row genuinely preserved; the table listed after LEFT JOIN only contributes its matching rows

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Swapping which table is written first in a LEFT JOIN genuinely changes which side gets fully preserved. The order you write the tables in is not just stylistic, it directly determines the actual behavior of the join.
6. Genuinely Common Mistakes

A few real patterns undermine left join usage. Confusing which table is genuinely the left table, especially in a query with several joins chained together. Filtering on a right table column in WHERE without an explicit NULL check, which can silently undo the entire point of using a left join in the first place.

And forgetting that NULL genuinely fills every selected right side column when no match exists, not just one specific column, which can surprise you if you expected only the join key itself to show NULL.

blocks.alt: Common mistakes: confusing which table is the left table, filtering on a right column without a NULL check, and forgetting NULL fills every right side column
